data.title: Divi's Lab net profit surges 63% to ₹1,127 cr in Q2
data.description:
Divi's Laboratories Ltd on Saturday posted a sharp 63.57 per cent rise in net profit to ₹1,127 crore in the September quarter due to higher revenues.

The company posted a net profit of ₹689 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, a regulatory filing said.

Revenue from operations rose 35.39 per cent to ₹3,676 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from ₹2,715 crore a year earlier, it said.

Its total expenses rose to ₹2,265 crore in the period under review from ₹1,948 crore a year ago, it added.

The company's net profit for the first half of the current fiscal year, however, declined 35.39 per cent to ₹2,029 crore from ₹2,568 crore in the year-ago period, the filing added.

data.title: HUT Stock Extends Losing Streak To Seven Weeks Despite Friday Rebound As Texas AI Data Center Concerns Mount
data.description:
Key points:
  • The company posted its Q3 revenue on Wednesday, and the revenue for the quarter was nearly $71 million.
  • This was down from $83.5 million in the same quarter last year.
  • Hut8 said it was targeting delivery of the first data hall at its River Bend campus by the second quarter of 2027. 

Hut 8 Corp. (HUT) stock posted its lowest weekly close in seven months on Friday, extending its losing streak to a seventh straight week.

This stock’s weekly close dropped more than 11%. That makes it the stock's worst close in a week since early April. Most of the slide came after the company reported third-quarter results on Wednesday.

The stock fell roughly 28% from Tuesday's close to Thursday's close.

HUT stock rebounded briefly, closing over 14% up on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HUT remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Why HUT Stock Was Under Pressure This Week

The selloff also comes amid political uncertainty in Texas, where Hut 8 is constructing its Beacon Point site. Investors' sentiment was impacted by the state's new governor may have on the project. According to an Investing.com report, the Democratic governor-elect campaigned on putting a freeze on new data center construction.

According to the report, the existing administration had already halted the permitting process in preparation for a December audit. On Thursday, many Wall Street firms lowered their price forecasts for Hut 8, citing concerns about permitting risks at the 1,000-megawatt Nueces County facility.

Revenue Falls Short Of Estimates

Hut 8's revenue for the quarter was nearly $71 million, down from $83.5 million in the same quarter last year. The company also reported a loss of $1.23 per share. The company said net income stood at $189.5 million. That also includes $413.8 million in mostly unrealized gains on its Bitcoin (BTC) and digital asset holdings. The value of the tokens still held by Hut 8 has risen instead of in cash from the sale, creating unrealized gains.

Bitcoin Sales Fund Buybacks

The company said unrestricted cash declined to $156.9 million from $233.6 million. Separately, the company sold around 954 Bitcoin, raising $74.8 million in cash in the process.

In October, it sold another 2,148 Bitcoins for $175.4 million. The filing also showed that $250 million went to buybacks. The company said Hut 8's board approved an additional $750 million in buybacks. That increased the total authorization to $1 billion.

Hut 8 Targets 2027 Launch For AI Data Centers

Hut 8 has been shifting its focus from Bitcoin mining to the construction of data centers for artificial intelligence. The company said it is targeting delivery of the first data hall at its River Bend campus in the second quarter of 2027.

Until then, its compute business is still driving the top line. The company said the unit, which includes Bitcoin mining and cloud services, generated $68.4 million of the quarter's revenue.

data.title: Muhurat trading 2026: Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi sees Sensex at 1,00,000 next Diwali? Shares 3 Samvat 2083 stock picks
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Muhurat Trading 2026 | Sensex, Nifty 50 target in Samvat 2083: Following weakness in the US dollar, triggering profit-booking in the US bond market and cooling crude oil prices after the US Midterm Election Results 2026, the Indian stock market outperformed global markets. The Nifty 50 index finished at 25,030, logging a weekly gain of 8.60%, whereas the Bank Nifty index ended at 59,086, registering a weekly gain of over 8%. The BSE Sensex finished at 81,028, 6,569 points or 8.82% higher from the previous week's close.

As Dalal Street is ready for the special Muhurat Trading session 2026 on Sunday, 8 November 2026, from 2:20 PM to 3:30 PM, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083, market participants are expecting the Indian stock market's positive performance to repeat for the ninth straight session on Diwali 2026 date, i.e. 8 November 2026.

Ganesh Dongre, AVP - Equity Research at Anand Rathi, believes the Indian stock market bias has improved after the humiliating defeat of Donald Trump's Republican Party in the US Midterm Elections. The Anand Rathi expert said that the Democrats' sweeping victory has eased Middle East tensions, leading to a slump in crude oil prices. Dongre said that the US Midterm Election Results have put the US dollar under pressure, which triggered profit-booking in the US bond market.

Highlighting the top 3 triggers, which are expected to dictate the movement of post-US Midterm Election Results 2026, Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said, "Movement in the US bond yields, anti-AI trade and inflation are expected to dominate the movement of global equities, including Dalal Street."

The Anand Rathi expert said that a correction in US bond yields would trigger movement of smart money from the US bond market to equities and other assets. However, this won't have a long-term impact, as it would only trigger FPI money flow into the Indian stock market.

"Anti-AI trade and inflation hold key, as anti-AI trade is expected to accelerate the FPI's money flow towards the Indian stock market, and inflation remaining under control would mean less pressure on the central banks for further rate hikes. In fact, lowering of inflation may prompt the global central banks to move towards a lower interest rate regime, providing enough domestic liquidity in the market," said Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi.

However, the Anand Rathi expert advised investors to remain vigilant about the US economy after the US Midterm Elections. He said that the US economy is already under pressure and that the policy paralysis following the US Midterm Election Results is expected to worsen further. In such a scenario, if the US economy continues to nose-dive, the fundamentals may change.

Speaking on the outlook for the key benchmark indices of the Indian stock market, Ganesh Dongre said, "Despite heavy selling by FIIs, the DIIs have lent strong support to the Indian stock market in the last two years. Now, as global sentiment improves and FPIs are expected to pump money into emerging markets, including Dalal Street, we expect at least 20% upside in the 50-stock index. So, the Nifty 50 index is expected to be above 30,000 by next Diwali."

On the Sensex target in 2027, Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said, "The Sensex remains 3-3.5 times the Nifty 50 index. As the Nifty 50 index is expected to be above 30,000, the BSE Sensex can be expected to be above 90,000 in the base case and around 1,05,000 in the bull case."

On stocks to buy during the Muhurat trading session 2026, Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi recommended these three Samvat 2083 stock picks: Reliance Industries, Eternal, and ICICI Bank.

2] Eternal: Buy at Rs.363 | Target Rs.440 | Stop-loss Rs.320; and

data.title: Why Deepinder Goyal's Temple is drawing social media scrutiny
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal's wearable device Temple is navigating a social media storm, as doctors demand to know its scientific basis while Goyal defends his product as a fitness tracker and wellness product.

The bean-shaped gadget, worn close to one's temple, is claimed to track signals associated with brain activity and blood flow. It also claims to detects patterns such as auto chewing detection, snoring patterns and sleep patterns. Priced at Rs.85,000, Temple is not yet available to the public, although the company has opened pre-orders. For now, the device is being used by a select group of early users, including investors and people associated with Goyal.

"We are not a medical device. If at some point we clinically validate any of our metrics, we will let you know," said a 5 November X post from Goyal, who has raised investments of $54 million for Temple, including from InfoEdge Ventures, Peak XV, Vijay Shekhar Sharma and Varun Alagh.

Mint spoke with medical experts, early users of the device and lawyers to understand the controversy.

Vikram Chopra, co-founder of Cars24 and an angel investor in Temple, has been using the device for two months. Chopra said the accompanying app displays several metrics similar to those offered by other fitness wearables, including sleep quality and resting heart rate.

"I use Polar, which is considered the gold standard, especially during exercise. It is a chest strap used by athletes around the world. Temple compares very well with it. I also use Whoop, a screenless, wrist-worn fitness tracker," he said.

In a post on X on 1 November, Goyal claimed that Temple recorded more accurate heart-rate readings than Whoop, Fitbit and Oura Ring in an internal study.

Doctors question whether a sensor placed near the temple can accurately measure blood circulation inside the brain.

"Temple appears to be measuring blood flow in the superficial temporal artery, which supplies blood to the scalp, not the brain. The brain receives blood through the internal carotid and vertebral arteries. These are not the same. Blood flow through the superficial temporal artery does not necessarily reflect blood flow inside the brain," said Dr. Kapil Singhal, director of neurology at the Institute of Neurosciences, Medanta, Noida.

One contentious claim relates to Entropy, which Goyal describes as a new biomarker tracked by Temple, measuring the body's real-time energy expenditure, or the metabolic cost of keeping the body alive.

Doctors and other experts have questioned the scientific basis of the metric, particularly as users are encouraged to lower their Entropy scores for a longer life. They argue that health and longevity recommendations should not be based on a metric that has not been independently validated.

Eternal did not respond to Mint's queries.

"I am excited about the new understanding of the human body that an instrument like this will unlock for humanity. We have a number of new research breakthroughs coming up (especially Entropy), and are validating them as we speak," Goyal wrote on X on 6 November.

"Independent validation is important to establish what actually works and what does not. We cannot simply glorify something that may not work, but neither should we dismiss it without examining it," said Dr. Ponniah Vanamoorthy, head and senior consultant, neuroanesthesiology & neurocritical care, Kauvery Hospital, Chennai.

Some have gone to the extent of calling it a gimmick. "If Temple is not a medical device, then why is Goyal addressing the medical community and seeking peer validation? It could simply be an accessory, like an iPhone that tracks your steps and other parameters. I would call it a gimmick because there are no studies to support the claims being made," said Dr. Kadam Nagpal, senior consultant, neurology, Salubritas Medcentre.

Meanwhile, legal experts argue that describing Temple as a fitness or wellness device is not conclusive of its regulatory classification. If Temple is intended to measure or investigate cerebral blood flow, there is an arguable basis for treating it as a medical device, since cerebral blood flow is a physiological process.

"However, measuring a physiological parameter does not automatically make a product a medical device. The determination would depend on its intended purpose, the nature of the measurements and the manufacturer's representations," said Ketan Mukhija, partner and co-head, PE and VC Practice at Kochhar & Co.

This is not the first time Goyal has faced criticism from the scientific community. In November 2025, he drew scrutiny for proposing the Gravity Ageing Hypothesis, which suggests that Earth's gravitational pull could contribute to human ageing by gradually affecting blood flow to the brain. Doctors refuted the claim, stating there is no established scientific evidence to support the proposition.

"Blood flow to the brain is slightly lower when we stand than when we lie down, and it declines with age. Lower brain blood flow is also associated with cognitive decline. But the leap is to say that decades of standing upright cause brain ageing. There is no established evidence for that. The brain tightly regulates its own blood supply, and the association with age could run the other way: an ageing brain may simply need and receive less blood," said Dr. Anshul Sadhale, founder of FreeGymAI.

data.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files draft papers with SEBI for IPO
data.description:
New Delhi: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), backed by The Coca-Cola Company and Jubilant Beverages, has filed its draft papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).

The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99,74,61,456 equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6.

Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO, with the entire proceeds going to the selling shareholder.

data.title: Astronomers spot white dwarf star with two rings of planetary debris
data.description:
Key points:
  • White dwarf located roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth
  • Debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration
  • Our solar system may have same fate in distant future

By Will Dunham

Billions of years from now, the sun is expected to run out of fuel and greatly expand into what is called a red giant, eventually shedding its outer layers and leaving behind its dense core, a white dwarf. Some of the planets in our solar system would be destroyed while others might survive.

Researchers have now spotted a white dwarf with planetary debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration that may offer a peek into one possible outcome for our solar system in the distant future.

Unlike in similar systems previously observed, the debris disc surrounding this white dwarf appears to consist of two distinct rings. The researchers said the disc may have been shaped by two planetary or smaller rocky bodies that are embedded in the rings after managing to survive the star's violent death throes.

The white dwarf, named J1328−1450, is located in the Milky Way roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth, in the constellation Virgo. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). The observations were made using the European Southern Observatory's Chile-based Very Large Telescope.

Prior to this discovery, astronomers had identified 21 white dwarfs with debris surrounding them, all of which had a single disc and not a double ring of material as the new observations reveal.

"It shows that the remnants of a planetary system can have a much more complex structure than we previously thought, and provides further support to the idea that planetary rocky bodies may survive the transformation of a star into a white dwarf," said astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches of Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María in Chile, one of the authors of the study published in the journal Nature Astronomy.

The white dwarf has a mass about 47% that of the sun, jam-packed into a diameter roughly the same as that of Earth.

The surviving planetary bodies may be remnants of larger and heavily disrupted planets. One of them may be around the size of the dwarf planet Pluto, with the other one smaller than that.

Lagos-Vilches said the original star may have hosted a planetary system before it expanded dramatically into a red giant, engulfing some of the innermost planets while ones with more distant orbits survived.

"The planetary system did not completely disappear. Some surviving rocky bodies may have been gravitationally perturbed onto highly eccentric orbits that brought them close to the white dwarf," Lagos-Vilches said.

"Objects that came sufficiently close were disrupted by the white dwarf's gravitational force. Their material was spread into a debris disc containing dust and gas. However, two relatively large rocky bodies may have survived within this debris," Lagos-Vilches said.

The presence of the two bodies may help explain the distribution of the surrounding material into a pair of concentric gaseous rings, Lagos-Vilches said.

"The outer ring is strongly depleted in magnesium compared with the inner ring. This suggests that they may originate from different parent bodies, or possibly from different layers of a rocky body that was disrupted when it went too close to the white dwarf due to its strong gravitational field," Lagos-Vilches said.

A GLIMPSE OF THE FUTURE

In about 5 billion years, the sun will become a red giant, Lagos-Vilches said.

"It will eventually lose its outer layers and become a white dwarf. The inner solar system will be dramatically affected. Mercury and Venus are expected to be engulfed by the expanding sun, while there is still no clear consensus on whether Earth will also be engulfed during this phase. The fate of the outer planets is different. Jupiter, Saturn and the more distant bodies should have a much better chance of surviving," Lagos-Vilches said.

After the sun becomes a white dwarf, surviving planetary remnants, moons and asteroids could potentially be drawn close enough to the white dwarf to be torn apart by gravitational forces.

"A debris disc like the one around J1328−1450 could therefore represent one possible stage in the very distant future of our own planetary system," Lagos-Vilches said.

data.title: Prism Reports Rs 353 Cr Profit In Q1 FY27, Revenue Rises 35%
data.description:
IPO-bound hospitality company PRISM, the parent entity of OYO, reported a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 353 Cr in the first quarter of FY27, marking a 17.3 per cent increase from Rs 301 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.

As per a media report, the profit growth was largely supported by a deferred tax credit of nearly Rs 244 Cr during the quarter.

PRISM's operating revenue rose 35 per cent to Rs 2,814 Cr in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 2,078 Cr in the year-ago period. The company's EBITDA also increased 24.3 per cent to Rs 760 Cr from Rs 611 Cr in Q1 FY26.

On the operational front, the company's gross booking value (GBV) stood at nearly Rs 9,600 Cr in the quarter ended June 2026, registering growth of around 30 per cent from Rs 7,408 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.

PRISM founder and CEO Ritesh Agarwal had earlier attributed the company's performance to improving gross margins and higher operating earnings across its hotel and vacation home businesses. He also highlighted investments in technology, brands and distribution capabilities as key contributors to the company's growth.

Founded in 2012 by Agarwal, OYO initially began as a budget hotel chain before expanding into holiday homes, coworking spaces, motels and corporate stays. The company now operates across more than 35 countries. Its parent entity, Oravel Stays, was rebranded as PRISM last year ahead of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The company has raised approximately USD 3.5 Bn to date, with investors including SoftBank, Lightspeed India, Peak XV Partners and Microsoft.

PRISM is preparing for its stock market debut after filing its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) through the confidential pre-filing route in December last year. It received regulatory approval for its IPO in June and subsequently filed an updated DRHP for a Rs 6,650 Cr public issue, comprising entirely of a fresh issue of shares.

The Ritesh Agarwal-led company is reportedly targeting a valuation of USD 7 Bn to USD 8 Bn for the proposed IPO.

data.title: Noel Tata To Retire As Titan Vice-Chairman On November 12
data.description:
Noel Tata's retirement from Titan's board follows the Tata Group's governance policy mandating retirement of non-executive, non-independent directors at 70

Noel N. Tata will step down as Vice-Chairman and Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director of Titan Company on November 12, 2026, upon attaining the age of 70, in accordance with the Tata Group's governance guidelines, the company said in a stock exchange filing.

In a disclosure dated November 5, Titan said Tata's retirement from the board would take effect at the close of business on November 12. The departure is in line with the group's governance policy, which sets 70 years as the retirement age for Non-Executive, Non-Independent Directors.

Tata joined Titan's board in March 2022 and has been associated with the Tata Group for more than four decades. He holds leadership positions across several group companies and is among the senior figures overseeing the conglomerate's businesses and philanthropic institutions.

He is currently Chairman of Trent, Voltas and Tata Investment Corporation, and Vice-Chairman of Tata Steel. He also serves as Chairman of Tata International and Tata Trusts.

His retirement from Titan's board does not, by itself, indicate any change in his positions at the other Tata Group companies. No corresponding retirement announcements from these companies have been established in the disclosures reviewed.

Tata's exit from Titan's board comes as the group continues to follow its governance framework governing board tenure and retirement of non-executive directors.

Titan, a Tata Group company, operates across jewellery, watches and wearables, and eyewear, with brands including Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane, Titan and Fastrack.

data.title: Uno Minda Elevates Kartikeya Joshi To CMO
data.description:
Joshi takes on the marketing leadership role after serving as President and Head of Corporate Planning and Group Strategy, bringing over 20 years of cross-sector experience

Uno Minda has elevated Kartikeya Joshi to Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), following his tenure as President and Head of Corporate Planning and Group Strategy at the company. Joshi brings over 20 years of experience across the automotive and health-tech sectors, with a career spanning corporate strategy, planning and business leadership.

Previous Role At Uno Minda

Before his elevation, Joshi served as President and Head of Corporate Planning and Group Strategy at Uno Minda. His appointment to the CMO role marks a shift from his previous focus on corporate planning and group strategy to marketing leadership.

The company has not disclosed further details about his new responsibilities or the scope of his marketing mandate.

Experience Across Sectors

Joshi has more than two decades of professional experience across the automotive and health-tech industries. His career includes roles at Curo Healthcare, Bosch Chassis Systems India, Philips, and Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions.

His experience across these organisations spans sectors with distinct business models and operating environments. His move into the CMO role brings his corporate planning and strategy experience to the company's marketing leadership.

Career Across Organisations

Before his latest elevation, Joshi held positions at several established companies, including Bosch Chassis Systems India and Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions. He also worked with Philips and Curo Healthcare, adding health-tech experience to his automotive-sector background.

His career progression at Uno Minda, from leading corporate planning and group strategy to taking on the CMO position, places him in a marketing leadership role at the company.

The appointment marks Joshi's latest career move after more than 20 years of experience across automotive and health-tech businesses.

data.title: STL Appoints Aviral Singh As Corporate HR Head
data.description:
Singh moves from Yokohama-ATG to lead corporate HR at STL, bringing experience in workforce planning, performance management and organisational development

Sterlite Technologies (STL) has appointed Aviral Singh as Corporate HR Head, effective October 2026. Singh joins the telecommunications and digital infrastructure company from Yokohama-ATG, where he most recently served as Associate Director and Head of HR Business Partnering. His experience spans corporate HR, manufacturing, talent management, compensation governance and global performance management.

HR Leadership At Yokohama-ATG

Before joining STL, Singh spent over four years at Yokohama-ATG, holding roles across HR business partnering and performance management. As Associate Director and Head of HR Business Partnering, he led the corporate office HR portfolio and coordinated central HR initiatives across manufacturing locations.

He managed a team of three senior HR business partners, overseeing people strategy and organisational effectiveness. His responsibilities included workforce planning, organisational design, succession planning, retention, compensation and leadership advisory.

Singh also led global performance management processes across India, the United States and Europe. His work included standardising goal-setting and performance calibration, overseeing annual salary reviews and conducting global compensation benchmarking.

Talent And Performance Management

Earlier, Singh served as Chief Manager, leading HR business partnering for corporate functions and the Off Highway and PCR businesses at Yokohama-ATG. He also worked as Senior Human Resources Manager, combining HR business partnering responsibilities with leadership of global performance management.

During these roles, he worked on succession planning, management trainee recruitment, employee lifecycle management and organisational development. He also contributed to job banding, grading, organisational restructuring and HR systems implementation.

His experience includes changes to performance evaluation processes, including the introduction of an absolute rating scale to replace the traditional bell-curve methodology.

Earlier Career Experience

Before Yokohama-ATG, Singh worked as an HR Business Partner at L&T Hydrocarbon Engineering from October 2019 to May 2022. His responsibilities covered manpower budgeting, talent management, employee engagement, performance management and recruitment planning.

He began his HR career at Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, where he served as Area HR Manager from July 2017 to October 2019. He managed HR operations for more than 1,200 employees across Mumbai, supporting recruitment, manpower deployment, succession planning and employee engagement.

Academic Background

Singh holds a Post Graduate Diploma in Management in Human Resource Management from KJ Somaiya Institute of Management Studies and Research, completed in 2017. He also holds a Bachelor of Engineering degree in Information Technology from Thakur College of Engineering and Technology.

His appointment adds experience in corporate HR, workforce planning and performance management to STL’s human resources leadership.

data.title: Green Finance Outpaces Fossil Fuel Deals In Bank Earnings For Fifth Year
data.description:
Global lenders generated nearly USD 3 billion in fees from climate-related debt transactions in 2026, marginally surpassing fossil fuel financing revenues, although the wider shift in capital allocation remains slow

Global banks have earned nearly USD 3 billion from arranging climate-related loans and bond transactions in 2026, surpassing the USD 2.9 billion generated from fossil fuel financing for the fifth consecutive year, highlighting the growing commercial importance of sustainable finance in global banking. According to data compiled by Bloomberg, lenders generated approximately USD 3 billion in fees from climate-linked debt deals, including financing for environmentally friendly projects, compared with revenues from arranging debt transactions for oil, gas and coal producers.

The figures indicate a continuing shift in banking revenues towards green financing, although the gap between the two segments remains narrow. The trend marks a significant reversal from 2020, when banks earned almost twice as much from fossil fuel financing as they did from supporting green initiatives. The latest figures suggest that climate finance is increasingly becoming an established revenue stream for financial institutions rather than remaining a niche segment of the lending market.

Green Debt Drives Banking Revenues

Bank of China, BNP Paribas and Deutsche Bank emerged as the leading revenue generators from underwriting green bonds since the beginning of the year, according to Bloomberg data. In the green loan segment, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Credit Agricole and Societe Generale recorded the highest revenues from arranging financing transactions. The growing demand for capital to support renewable energy, electricity grids, energy storage and other low-carbon infrastructure is creating fresh business opportunities for lenders.

Governments, utilities and corporates are increasingly approaching financial institutions to raise funds for energy transition projects, providing banks with opportunities to generate underwriting and loan arrangement fees. However, fossil fuel financing continues to remain commercially significant. US lenders, including Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup, were among the biggest dealmakers in oil, gas and coal-related bond and loan transactions. This indicates that financial institutions are expanding their green financing portfolios without completely withdrawing from traditional energy markets, creating a dual-track business model.

Capital Allocation Remains Uneven

Despite the growing revenues from green financing, the wider allocation of capital towards low-carbon infrastructure remains insufficient to meet global climate objectives. Data show that the ratio of spending on low-carbon infrastructure relative to fossil fuels increased to 0.97 in 2025, compared with 0.95 in 2024. However, the ratio needs to reach 4:1 by 2030 to align with climate goals. Analysts have cautioned that progress remains gradual and significantly below the pace required to achieve climate targets. Regional differences further underline the uneven transition.

China's energy supply banking ratio increased to 1.6:1, supported by higher grid-related debt issuance, while Europe's ratio reached 2.5:1, driven partly by offshore wind project financing.

North America, in contrast, recorded a decline to 0.5:1 as financing for oil, gas and coal increased.

For global banks, the emerging trend presents both an opportunity and a challenge. While green debt is becoming an increasingly attractive source of fee income, continued exposure to fossil fuel financing could invite greater scrutiny from investors and regulators. The next phase of sustainable banking will depend on whether rising green finance revenues translate into a meaningful reallocation of capital towards low-carbon infrastructure.

data.title: AI, Data And Cybersecurity Drive 30.3% Of GCC Tech Hiring Demand
data.description:
Quess Corp report finds a 4.5 percentage point rise in demand for advanced technology skills in Q2 FY27, while tier II cities gain momentum

Artificial intelligence (AI), data and cybersecurity accounted for 30.3 per cent of technology hiring demand at India's Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the July-September quarter of 2026, up from 25.8 per cent in the preceding quarter, according to a report by Quess Corp. The findings point to a growing focus on specialised technology skills, even as talent shortages and concentration of advanced-skill hiring in major cities remain challenges.

The India GCC Tech Talent Landscape – Q2 FY27 Report identifies supply gaps of 38-42 per cent in AI, data and analytics, and 30-35 per cent in cybersecurity and risk management. It also found that 87-88 per cent of advanced-skill hiring remained concentrated in tier I cities.

Demand For Advanced Skills

The report recorded a 4.5 percentage point quarter-on-quarter increase in the combined share of AI, data and cybersecurity in technology hiring demand. The trend reflects GCCs' growing need for professionals who can deploy AI applications, manage data infrastructure and strengthen enterprise security.

Quess Corp identified transitions from adjacent roles as one way to address talent shortages. These include data scientists moving into model operations, data engineers shifting towards applied AI and cybersecurity analysts developing expertise in cloud security.

Structured reskilling and internal career pathways could complement external recruitment as demand for advanced technology capabilities expands across sectors, the report said.

Tier II Cities Gain Ground

Coimbatore recorded approximately 30 per cent quarter-on-quarter growth in GCC technology hiring demand during the July-September quarter. The city contributed to overall tier II hiring growth of 13 per cent, compared with 8-10 per cent in the first quarter of FY27.

The findings indicate that smaller cities are gaining traction in technology recruitment, although the bulk of demand remains concentrated in established hubs.

Metro Hiring Remains Uneven

Among tier I cities, Pune was the only market to record growth, with hiring demand increasing by 2 per cent quarter-on-quarter. Other major metropolitan markets experienced declines.

Hyderabad and Mumbai recorded the steepest falls, at approximately 10 per cent and 9 per cent, respectively. Despite the contraction, tier I cities continued to account for around 84-86 per cent of total GCC hiring demand.

Addressing Talent Shortages

The report highlights the need to combine specialised recruitment with workforce development to address persistent skill gaps. Internal mobility and targeted training could help organisations build capabilities while reducing dependence on an already constrained external talent pool.

Quess Corp Chief Executive Officer – IT Staffing Kapil Joshi said India's GCC ecosystem was expanding while the skills required by companies were changing, with AI, data and cybersecurity accounting for 30.3 per cent of technology hiring demand in the second quarter of FY27.

The report draws on secondary data, job postings across multiple employment platforms and information available in the public domain.

data.title: Diwali Fireworks! Nifty surges over 8% in Nov 2-6 week, best in 6 yrs after US Midterm Election results; RIL soars 13%
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- The Diwali festival arrived early on Dalal Street as Indian equities extended their winning streak to seven consecutive sessions, supported by US midterm election results, strong foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows, easing crude oil prices and robust Q2FY27 corporate earnings.

The rally helped the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 clock one of their sharpest weekly gains in recent years. A global sell-off in AI-linked stocks and softening US bond yields further lifted investor sentiment ahead of Diwali 2026.

The Nifty50 surged 8.58% during the week, gaining nearly 1,978 points to reclaim the 25,000 mark. This was its biggest weekly percentage gain in about six years, since January 2021, and its largest-ever weekly advance in absolute terms. The Sensex rallied nearly 9% to close above 81,000.

The rally added nearly Rs.28 lakh crore to investors' wealth, with the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies rising from Rs.475.34 lakh crore to around Rs.503 lakh crore.

Among the top gainers, Shriram Finance led with a nearly 17% rise, followed by Bajaj Finance and M&M, which gained over 15% each. HDFC Bank jumped around 14%, while Reliance Industries (RIL) added over 13%.

Meanwhile, on Friday, the Sensex surged 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to 81,028, while the Nifty gained 493.75 points, or 2.01%, to settle at 25,030. The rally came despite a sharp sell-off across global markets.

All eyes will now be on Diwali Muhurat trading on Sunday, November 8, 2026, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. The special session will be held from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm, with investors looking to make auspicious investments on Diwali.

The sharp recovery came after months of selling pressure through much of August, September and October, amid escalating tensions in West Asia and concerns over their impact on global energy prices.

"Indian equities defied a global rout, extending their winning run as investors treated the home market as a relative safe harbour amid turmoil abroad," said Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments. He added, "A sharp weekly slide in crude, easing U.S. Treasury yields and a firmer rupee further burnished India's relative appeal. With Fed officials still hinting at further hikes, the U.S. jobs report due later today will be closely watched."

One key factor supporting Indian equities was the sharp reversal in global technology stocks. The Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections fuelled concerns that tighter regulatory scrutiny could slow data centre expansion and curb AI infrastructure investments.

This triggered an anti-AI trade, wiping around $2.5 trillion off US stock market value on Thursday as technology stocks erased Wall Street's post-election rally. Asian markets, particularly those exposed to the AI supply chain, also came under pressure amid fears of regulatory intervention and slower infrastructure spending.

For India, this shift could be beneficial as investors reassess expensive AI-linked markets and consider Indian equities as an alternative, supported by recent outperformance and improving earnings.

Crude oil provided further relief. Brent crude fell nearly 16% during the week to around US$98 per barrel as concerns over the West Asia conflict eased. This is significant for India, which imports roughly 85% of its crude requirements.

Hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough raised expectations of fewer supply disruptions. US President Donald Trump discussed de-escalation with Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani, while Iran was reportedly reviewing proposals from mediators on its nuclear programme. However, uncertainty persisted, with Iran demanding the lifting of the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen assets before fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Furthermore, the rupee recovered around 0.50%, moving above the 94.00 mark, supported by FII buying and improving foreign fund flows.

FIIs infused around Rs.31,000 crore into Indian equities through the NSE between Monday and Thursday, reversing record outflows in September and October. On Thursday, they bought nearly Rs.15,000 crore worth of equities, their biggest single-day purchase in over a year, according to provisional exchange data. This followed months of selling that had pushed foreign ownership of Indian equities to historic lows.

VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said FIIs had purchased equities worth Rs.35,781 crore over the past five trading sessions.

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, continued selling and booking profits. However, Vijayakumar believes markets can remain resilient as long as foreign buying continues amid the changed global market construct.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - research, Religare Broking noted that following the sharp seven-session rally, some consolidation and sectoral rotation would be healthy.

"The Nifty's ability to sustain above 24,500 will be important to preserve the positive momentum and pave the way towards the 25,200-25,500 zone. We recommend maintaining a selective positive bias, focusing on fundamentally strong stocks demonstrating relative strength, while keeping position sizes in check amid potential volatility arising from global developments," he added.

data.title: Force Motors to launch EV on Traveller platform in Q4 FY27
data.description:
Force Motors plans to launch an electric model on its Traveller platform in the January-March period next year, according to a senior company official.

An electric ambulance is expected to be among the first set of offerings.

Electric vehicles on the Traveller platform have been developed and are undergoing final testing and homologation, Managing Director Prasan Firodia told PTI.

"We are scheduled to launch our electric vehicles on the Traveller platform in the first quarter of next calendar year," he said without disclosing further details.

"Our Traveller electric vehicles are currently under homologation. So, they are already developed. They are under homologation with ARAI and under final testing. Force Motors had showcased an electric variant of Traveller at the Auto Expo in 2024, but has not started sales yet."

The company plans to introduce multiple Traveller EV variants, followed by an electric version of its Urbania people carrier.

Urbania EV is under development and has a few months remaining before homologation, he said, adding that it plans to electrify its other platforms in stages.

Firodia said electric vehicle adoption in the passenger-carrier segment, particularly vehicles under seven metres, is still at an early stage and the pace of adoption would be gradual.

He said the economics has to work for customers, while range limitations and charging infrastructure remain major hurdles for vehicles used on varied routes.

"I do not expect that the EV transition for us will be something very rapid like what you have seen in passenger cars or the significant transition that has taken place in two-wheelers or three-wheelers. In our segment, transition will happen, but it will be a slow transition comparatively," he said.

According to him, school transport could be the one to shift to electric vehicles sooner because routes and daily distances are more predictable.

Vehicles used for tourism and travel can cover changing routes, making operating costs and charging needs harder to estimate.

The Traveller range serves healthcare, education, employee transport, tourism and other passenger-transport uses. Its applications include ambulances, school buses, police vans and delivery vehicles.

He also said Urbania had become a significant platform for the company in volume and revenue.

Meanwhile, Force Motors is investing ₹3,000 crore across capacity, engineering, electrification, hybrid driveline technology and digitisation, Firodia said.

The company is ramping up production capacity to 85,000 vehicles, he added.

data.title: SoftBank, ABB explore China carve-out to salvage robotics deal, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
Japan's SoftBank and Swiss engineering group ABB are looking at carving out the Chinese element of a $5.4 billion robotics deal which was blocked earlier this week by Beijing, Bloomberg News reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

SoftBank did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours and ABB declined to comment on the report which said that a carve-out would mean setting up a separate entity for the China business with different ownership.

This is the second deal blocked by China this year after Meta was ordered in April to unwind its more than $2 billion acquisition of AI startup Manus, as Beijing tightens scrutiny of foreign investment involving frontier technologies.

ABB is also considering other options including finding another buyer, the report said, adding that the business could potentially be valued at $2 billion to $3 billion.

China is ABB's biggest robotics market and accounts for about 30% of its robotics business. It operates about 30 local companies in China with around 15,000 employees in nearly 130 cities, as well as online and offline channels in nearly 700.

data.title: Coca-Cola's India bottler Hindustan Coca-Cola files for IPO
data.description:
Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings, India's largest Coca-Cola bottler, has filed for an initial public offering consisting entirely of a stake sale by its majority shareholder, with no fresh money going to the company, draft papers showed.

  • The proposed IPO will see majority shareholder Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings offer up to 997.5 million shares for sale, reducing its holding to about 45% from 60%.

  • Jubilant Beverages, which owns the remaining 40%, is not selling shares. No price band was disclosed.

  • The IPO ‌adds ⁠to a string of multinational companies turning to Indian equity markets to monetise their investments, rather than raise new capital.

  • The company's revenue fell 9.4% to 115.49 billion Indian rupees ($1.23 billion) in the year to March 2026. The company attributed the decline to the transfer of territories to other Coca-Cola bottlers under its refranchising programme.

  • The company bottles Coca-Cola brands including Thums Up, Sprite and Maaza across 10 Indian states and four federal territories, mainly in southern and western India.

  • Reuters reported in July that Coca-Cola had appointed JPMorgan and Citi for a planned 2027 listing. The draft prospectus names six banks managing the offer.

data.title: Gary Marcus Warns OpenAI Could Become ‘WeWork Of AI’ — And Nvidia May Pay The Price
data.description:
Key points:
  • Marcus drew comparisons with WeWork, pointing to OpenAI's repeatedly delayed IPO plans as a potential warning sign.
  • He noted that WeWork never completed its IPO, while OpenAI continues to push its own listing plans back.
  • Marcus added that the bigger concern, however, is what happens if OpenAI cannot sustain its current valuation and is forced to seek an alternative.

NYU Professor Emeritus Gary Marcus believes that OpenAI's ambitions and delayed IPO plans are raising uncomfortable questions about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

During an interview with CNBC, Marcus warned that growing skepticism around generative AI, rising financing costs and questions about whether companies can monetize their investments could expose vulnerabilities across the AI ecosystem.

He added that the company could become a cautionary tale for the industry, with potentially wider consequences for Nvidia Corp. (NVDA).

OpenAI Could Become The 'WeWork of AI,' Marcus Warns

Marcus questioned whether OpenAI's business trajectory can live up to the expectations surrounding it. Drawing a comparison with WeWork, the once high-flying office-sharing company that never went public, he pointed to OpenAI's repeatedly delayed IPO plans as a potential warning sign.

"OpenAI, for example, I've long talked about as possibly being the WeWork of AI," Marcus said.

He noted that WeWork never completed its IPO, while OpenAI continues to push its own listing plans back. Marcus added that the bigger concern, however, is what happens if OpenAI cannot sustain its current valuation and is forced to seek an alternative.

"What if OpenAI is forced to sell at a discount to something like Microsoft?" Marcus asked. He then raised the potential consequences for Nvidia, whose chips have powered much of the industry's AI infrastructure spending.

"What would be the effect on Nvidia of that if they're kind of poster child had to take a big hit," he said.

Nvidia's Biggest AI Risk May Be Whether Customers Can Make Money

Marcus believes Nvidia's strong technology and execution do not necessarily guarantee that demand for its chips will continue growing indefinitely.

"I think Nvidia is very well run. The chips are great, but there's a question about whether there's infinite demand and whether the companies buying it can make a profit from it," he said.

He also warned that the AI infrastructure boom could face a financing crunch, particularly among neocloud companies that depend heavily on external funding to expand their computing capacity.

"I think the neoclouds are the most vulnerable here. They need the financing. The financing is getting more expensive. They're in trouble," Marcus said.

The risk, he added, is that financial stress among these companies could spread across the broader AI ecosystem, including Nvidia.

Beyond financing, Marcus questioned whether the enormous investments in AI infrastructure are translating into meaningful productivity gains. Citing a Bank of England study involving approximately 10,000 decision-makers, he said the findings pointed to limited productivity improvements so far. Ultimately, he suggested that changing investor sentiment could prove just as important as financial fundamentals.

"To the extent that people lose faith in generative AI as being a rocket that hurts a company like Nvidia," Marcus said.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.17%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 0.21%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged up by 0.06%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) rose 1.32% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) gained 1.31%.

data.title: Indonesian workers rally for Prabowo as women march against president
data.description:
Hundreds of workers rallied in support of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Saturday amid allegations that police illegally wiretapped him, while hundreds of women marched against the president's policies.

The pro-Prabowo demonstration marked a contrast to recent protests against his administration, part of growing public discontent over his costly populist policies, handling of raging wildfires and weakening investor confidence in Southeast Asia's biggest economy.

Labour Party Chairperson Said Iqbal, leading the workers' rally, called for unity to support Prabowo and said he would mobilise union members against those who threaten the former general's presidency.

"We can mobilise members of our organisation across every town, every factory," Said, a special adviser to the president, was quoted as saying by Detik News. "We are prepared to respond at any moment to maintain order should any unrest arise, whether instigated by foreign interests or by individuals seeking to cause trouble."

Indonesian police have named four senior police officials as suspects accused of attempting to intercept Prabowo's communications, including a former police chief who is known as a loyalist of former President Joko Widodo.

The scandal has exposed deepening cracks between Prabowo and his predecessor and former backer, known as Jokowi.

Jokowi has said he respected the legal process. The lawyer for one of the four suspect said his client would cooperate with the investigation.

Also on Saturday civil society groups held the women's march in Jakarta to demand more women's rights and protest against Prabowo's handling of the forest fires that have been raging for months, his costly free-meal programme and a tax on women's sanitary products.

There have been several protests launched against Prabowo in recent months including student rallies last week in the capital and other cities.
